record.paper_title: Open problems in membrane computing and how not to solve them
record.original_question: For polynomial-time cell-like P systems with active membranes, what is the complexity-theoretic power as a function of division depth? In particular, after division depth 0 characterizes P, division depth 1 characterizes P^#P, and polynomial division depth characterizes PSPACE, does increasing any fixed constant division depth d to d + 1 form a proper hierarchy with matching upper bounds, and what class is obtained at intermediate depths such as O(log n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider recognizer cell-like P systems with active membranes operating in polynomial time (confluent semantics). The structure of such a system is a rooted tree of nested membranes, each labeled and possibly polarized, containing multisets of objects that evolve in parallel by maximally parallel application of rules of the standard types: object evolution, send-in and send-out communication, dissolution, and membrane division (elementary and possibly non-elementary). A uniform family {Π_n} of such P systems decides a language L if, on input of size n, Π_n halts in polynomially many steps and outputs acceptance iff the input is in L.

For a P system Π define its division depth as the maximum, over all computations and over all membranes ever created by division rules, of the nesting depth at which a division rule is applied. For a function d: ℕ → ℕ let PMC_AM(d) denote the class of languages decided in polynomial time by uniform families of confluent recognizer P systems with active membranes whose division depth on input of size n is at most d(n).

It is known that:
 (i) PMC_AM(0) = P,
 (ii) PMC_AM(1) = P^{#P},
 (iii) PMC_AM(poly(n)) = PSPACE.

Questions:
(a) For every fixed constant d ≥ 1, is PMC_AM(d) ⊊ PMC_AM(d+1), i.e., does division depth induce a proper infinite hierarchy at constant depths, and what are matching upper bounds characterizing PMC_AM(d) for each constant d ≥ 2?
(b) Characterize PMC_AM(d(n)) for intermediate growth rates such as d(n) = O(log n): which standard complexity class (if any) does it equal?
artifact.status_search_result: The endpoint characterizations (division depth 0 = P, depth 1 = P^{#P}, polynomial depth = PSPACE) are established in the membrane-computing literature, but no published characterization of the intermediate constant-depth classes or of logarithmic division depth appears to exist; the question of whether constant division depth yields a proper hierarchy with matching upper bounds is listed as an open problem in surveys on P systems with active membranes.

status_evidence.title: Membrane Division, Oracles, and the Counting Hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: Elementary (leaf) membrane division gives computing power P^{#P}.

status_evidence.title: P Systems with Active Membranes Characterize PSPACE
status_evidence.snippet: Confluent recognizer P systems with active membranes solve exactly PSPACE in polynomial time.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial division depth corresponds to PSPACE.

status_evidence.title: Shallow Non-confluent P Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of how membrane nesting depth affects computational power of P systems.
status_evidence.claim: Intermediate division depths remain to be characterized.
